<span class="badge status-score-bearing">score-bearing</span>

> Uses a versioned hard MNIST split, classwise anomaly AUROC, and explicit no-training controls with a compact local autoencoder. This preserves the train-on-normal and score-by-reconstruction-error shape of the MLPerf Tiny anomaly-detection workload while requiring a measurable benefit from training.

## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload anomaly-ae-train --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-ae-train --profile max --open-report

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-ae-train --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload anomaly-ae-train --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

| **Repeatability metric** | sample coefficient of variation of train_and_eval_seconds across the five reference runs |
| **Repeatability limit** | 0.05 |
| **Repeatability action** | withhold the performance reference and rerun the complete protocol when the coefficient of variation exceeds 5% |
| **Artifact policy** | preserve JSON, HTML, CSV, .provd.json, run fingerprint, dataset asset metadata, and raw metric values for each run |
| **Rerun policy** | rerun all five references when model code, dataset preprocessing, optimizer schedule, PyTorch major version, or target hardware class changes |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The primary score is a macro average, and the independent worst-class gate prevents an easy anomaly digit from hiding a weak one. Reconstruction MSE remains diagnostic only.
- The learned-control gate proves that optimization added discrimination beyond a zero reconstructor, a normal-data centroid, and the seeded untrained architecture.
